parts.prompt_markdown: Calculate unbiased estimates for the population mean and variance of \(X\).
State a necessary condition for the estimates found in part (a) to be reliable.

skills: calculate unbiased estimates for population mean and variance from summary statistics
methods: use formulas for unbiased estimators based on n, Σx and Σx^2

questions.stem_markdown:
The lengths, \(X\) cm, of a sample of 100 insects of a certain type were summarised as follows.

\[
n = 100 \quad \sum x = 36.8 \quad \sum x^2 = 17.34
\]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Oe.
For use of a correct formula (ft *their* $\mu$).

E.g. - Values must have been randomly selected. - Sample should be representative of the population. - All values should have equal chance of being selected. - It should be an unbiased sample. - Independent sample/insect lengths are independent of one another. ISW

parts.prompt_markdown: Calculate an approximate 98% confidence interval for the proportion of people living in Barapet who own a BETEC phone.

Manjit claims that more than 40% of the people living in Barapet own a BETEC phone.

Use your answer to part (a) to comment on this claim.

skills: construct an approximate confidence interval for a population proportion
compare a claim to the confidence interval to comment
methods: use normal approximation to the sampling distribution of the sample proportion
interpret results relative to the claimed threshold

questions.stem_markdown: A random sample of 250 people living in Barapet was chosen. It was found that 78 of these people owned a BETEC phone.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Use of a correct formula (any $z$).
Must be an interval.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Unlikely to be true because confidence interval does not contain 0.4.
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: FT their confidence interval. Must include this reason and ‘unlikely’, oe. Allow “not true because 0.4 is not in the confidence interval.” But “Confidence interval only goes up to 0.38 so not true” and “it’ lies outside the confidence interval” both score B0.

parts.prompt_markdown: Use a suitable approximating distribution to find the probability that at least 3 of the tickets sold by the agent are prize-winning tickets.
Justify the use of your approximating distribution in this context.

skills: use an appropriate approximating distribution to compute a probability for a count
justify the approximation using event rarity and independence assumptions
methods: model number of prize-winning tickets as Poisson(λ) with λ based on expected count
use Poisson distribution to evaluate tail probability

questions.stem_markdown: In a certain lottery, on average 1 in every 10 000 tickets is a prize-winning ticket. An agent sells 6000 tickets.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Mean = 0.6 seen.
Any $$\lambda$$ Allow one end error. Must see expression. Accept correct $$\Sigma$$ notation.
**SC** 0.0231 and no working scores B1 (could be implied). **SC** use of binomial scores M1A1 for 0.0231.
Must state values of $$n$$ and either $$np$$ or $$p$$. Note: ‘$$n$$ large, $$p$$ small’ is insufficient.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the probability that in a randomly chosen year the firm uses more gasoline than diesel fuel.

The costs per litre of gasoline and diesel fuel are \($0.80\) and \($0.85\) respectively.

Find the probability that the total cost of gasoline and diesel fuel in a randomly chosen year is between \($20\,000\) and \($22\,000\).

skills: compute probability that one normal variable exceeds another
compute probability that the sum (or weighted sum) of independent normal variables lies in a given interval
methods: model total cost as a linear combination and standardise using mean and variance
subtopics: linear combinations of independent normal variables

questions.stem_markdown: Each year a transport firm uses \(X\) litres of gasoline and \(Y\) litres of diesel fuel, where \(X\) and \(Y\) have the independent distributions \(X \sim N(10\,700, 950^2)\) and \(Y \sim N(13\,400, 1210^2)\).

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For standardising with *their* E and Var.
For area consistent with *their* values.
For one standardisation with *their* E and Var.
For area consistent with *their* values.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the probability that during a randomly chosen 2-day period no girls arrive late.
Find the probability that during a randomly chosen 5-day period the total number of students who arrive late is less than 3.

It is given that the values of \(P(G = r)\) and \(P(B = r)\) for \(r \geq 3\) are very small and can be ignored.
Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day more girls arrive late than boys.

Following a timetable change the teacher claims that on average more students arrive late than before the change. During a randomly chosen 5-day period a total of 4 students are late.

Test the teacher’s claim at the 5% significance level.

skills: calculate Poisson probabilities for no events over a period
find probability of the total count being below a threshold
estimate probability conditional on event counts using Poisson approximations/ignored tail probabilities
perform a hypothesis test at a given significance level for a Poisson rate/mean
methods: use Poisson(λt) with λ derived from given rates
use independence to sum Poisson variables
set up and conduct a significance test based on the null/alternative and chosen test statistic/critical region
subtopics: hypothesis test for Poisson mean/ rate using normal or exact approximation

questions.stem_markdown: A teacher models the numbers of girls and boys who arrive late for her class on any day by the independent random variables \(G \sim \text{Po}(0.10)\) and \(B \sim \text{Po}(0.15)\) respectively.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Accept $$e^{-0.2}$$ as final answer.
Any $$\lambda$$ Allow one end error. Must see expression (in any form). Accept correct $$\Sigma$$ notation.
**SC** Answer with no working seen scores B1 (could be implied).
P(B = 0) × P(G = 1) + P(B = 0) × P(G = 2) + P(B = 1) × P(G = 2). For the three Poisson terms added (must be from a complete attempt at all 3 terms).
For one expression seen.
For adding their expressions.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: H_{0}: $$\lambda = 1.25$$ or 0.25[per day] H_{1}: $$\lambda > 1.25$$ or 0.25[per day]
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Or $$\mu$$ or ‘population mean’.
Any $$\lambda$$. No end errors. Expression must be seen (in any form). Accept correct $$\Sigma$$ notation.
**SC** 0.0383 with no working scores B1.
For a valid comparison.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: [Reject H_{0}] ‘Hence there is sufficient evidence to suggest that the teacher’s claim is true’ or ‘There is sufficient evidence to suggest that more students are late on average’.
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: No contradictions. In context and not definite, e.g. not ‘More students are late’ or ‘Claim is correct’. Ft their 0.0383.

parts.prompt_markdown: Using only this information show that \(P(X > -1) = \frac{245}{256}\).

It is now given that, for \(x\) in a suitable domain,

\[
f(x) = k(12 + 4x - x^2), \text{ where } k \text{ is a constant.}
\]

Find the value of \(k\).

A different random variable \(X\) has probability density function \(g(x) = \frac{2}{9}(2 + x - x^2)\). The domain of \(X\) is all values of \(x\) for which \(g(x) \geq 0\).

Find Var(\(X\)).

skills: use symmetry and given probability to find another probability
use normalisation to find the constant k for a given pdf form
find variance of a random variable given its pdf
methods: apply symmetry about x=2 to relate tail probabilities
integrate the pdf over its support to set total probability 1
subtopics: symmetry of pdf about a vertical line
normalisation to find constant in pdf
finding probabilities and expectations from a pdf

questions.stem_markdown: The graph of the probability density function \(f\) of a random variable \(X\) is symmetrical about the line \(x = 2\). It is given that \(P(2 < X < 5) = \frac{117}{256}\).

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of symmetry about $$x = 2$$, oe. E.g. $$(1 - 2 \times \frac{117}{256}) \div 2$$ or $$\frac{1}{2} + \frac{117}{256}$$.
Any correct numerical expression seen leading to AG.
Attempt to integrate $$f(x)$$ with any limits.

Use of limits 2 and 5 and equating *their* integration attempt to $$\frac{117}{256}$$. Or limits –2 and 6 equated to 1. Or limits –1 and 6 equated to $$\frac{245}{256}$$. Or limits –1 to 5 equated to $$\frac{234}{256}$$. Oe. No mixed methods.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$[2 + x - x^2 = 0]$$ $$x = -1$$ and $$x = 2$$ seen or implied [Domain is $$-1 \leq x \leq 2$$]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Attempt to integrate $$x^2 g(x)$$ with any limits.
Subtract *their* mean^{2} from *their* $$\int x^2 g(x) dx$$ (both must be numerical).

parts.prompt_markdown: State the probability of a Type I error.

You should assume that the value of \(\sigma\) after 2004 remains at 6.95.

Given that the value of \(\mu\) this year is actually 164.91, find the probability of a Type II error.

skills: state probability of a Type I error for a specified significance level
calculate probability of a Type II error given the true mean and known standard deviation
methods: use critical region based on Z test for the mean under H0
compute Type II error probability as probability sample mean falls in acceptance region when mean is true value
subtopics: Type I and Type II errors
one-sided test for population mean with known variance
normal distribution test statistic for sample mean

questions.stem_markdown: The heights, in centimetres, of adult females in Litania have mean \(\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\). It is known that in 2004 the values of \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) were 163.21 and 6.95 respectively. The government claims that the value of \(\mu\) this year is greater than it was in 2004. In order to test this claim a researcher plans to carry out a hypothesis test at the 1% significance level. He records the heights of a random sample of 300 adult females in Litania this year and finds the value of the sample mean.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Note: $$x \leq 0.01$$ scores B0.
Accept any $$z$$ ($$\pm$$).
Accept 3 sf accuracy here.
For standardising 164.91 with their 164.14 (could be 163.21).
For area attempt consistent with their values.
Accept anything in range 0.0275 to 0.028[0].
